findings.issue_text: [Medium/security] CryptoIntegration.java:57 (detectProvider) — fail-fast behavior (IllegalStateException on multiple CryptoProviders) replaced by silently picking highest order() with ignored providers only logged at debug; ties broken by nondeterministic ServiceLoader iteration order could let a FIPS deployment silently run the non-FIPS provider; ignored providers should be logged at warn and equal-order ties rejected or resolved deterministically

[Medium/bug] ASN1Decoder.java:~57 (readSequence) — declared sequence length is never reconciled with bytes actually consumed: a child extending past the declared length makes length go negative and the loop exits silently accepting out-of-bounds data, and readLength() returning -1 (indefinite-length) skips the loop and silently returns an empty list; the parser should reject indefinite length and require length == 0 after the loop (fail closed on malformed DER)

[Low/performance] AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:~99 (concatenatedRSToASN1DER) — the two statements ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger); ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger); encode into freshly created buffers that are immediately discarded; this dead code from refactoring should be removed

[Low/bug] AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:~61 (getBouncyCastleProvider) — returns the provider of the JVM default KeyStore type (e.g., SUN/SunJCE), which is never BouncyCastle even when BC is on the classpath, violating the CryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() contract and giving callers like BouncyIntegration.init() a silently wrong provider

[Low/api] CryptoProvider.java:~39 — adding an abstract order() method to the public CryptoProvider interface is a source/binary breaking change for external custom implementations (compile failures or AbstractMethodError); a default method returning 0 would have preserved compatibility

[Low/bug] ASN1Decoder.java:~74 (readInteger) — a malformed zero-length INTEGER causes new BigInteger(bytes) to throw NumberFormatException (unchecked) instead of the IOException the parser API declares for malformed input; the error should be converted for consistent exception handling

[Low/test_gap] ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:~50 — the test reuses one default-sized (P-256) key pair for ES256/ES384/ES512 and only asserts rs→DER→rs round-trip self-consistency, never validating the DER against an independent implementation (e.g., BouncyCastle) or exercising key sizes matching each algorithm's signature length, so a systematically wrong but self-consistent encoder/decoder pair would pass

[Low/test_gap] CryptoIntegration.java — the new provider-selection logic (ordering by order(), single-provider case, multiple providers with distinct orders, tie-breaking) has no test coverage despite being a notable behavior change in provider resolution

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] ASN1Decoder.java:~74 (readInteger) — a malformed zero-length INTEGER causes new BigInteger(bytes) to throw NumberFormatException (unchecked) instead of the IOException the parser API declares for malformed input; the error should be converted for consistent exception handling

adjudication.rationale: In ASN1Decoder.readInteger(), the code reads the DER/ASN.1 length and then does `byte[] bytes = read(length); return new BigInteger(bytes);`. If the encoded INTEGER has a zero length (length == 0), `read(0)` returns an empty array and `new BigInteger(new byte[0])` throws an unchecked NumberFormatException. This violates the method’s declared/expected malformed-input signaling via IOException (and is inconsistent with other parse errors in the class that are wrapped as IOException/EOFException).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:~50 — the test reuses one default-sized (P-256) key pair for ES256/ES384/ES512 and only asserts rs→DER→rs round-trip self-consistency, never validating the DER against an independent implementation (e.g., BouncyCastle) or exercising key sizes matching each algorithm's signature length, so a systematically wrong but self-consistent encoder/decoder pair would pass

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s new test `ECDSAAlgorithmTest` creates a single EC key pair once in the constructor via `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` (no curve specified, typically default P-256) and then reuses it for `ES256`, `ES384`, and `ES512`. The test only checks that `asn1derToConcatenatedRS(sign, signatureLength)` → `concatenatedRSToASN1DER(...)` → `asn1derToConcatenatedRS(...)` returns the same concatenated bytes (`Assert.assertArrayEquals(rsConcat, rsConcat2)`), which can pass even if the encoder/decoder pair is systematically self-consistent but wrong. It also doesn’t ensure key sizes/curves match each algorithm’s expected signature length (e.g., ES512 expecting P-521-length R/S). This is a concrete, diff-grounded test inadequacy, not a proven product bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] CryptoIntegration.java — the new provider-selection logic (ordering by order(), single-provider case, multiple providers with distinct orders, tie-breaking) has no test coverage despite being a notable behavior change in provider resolution

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes CryptoIntegration.detectProvider() to sort discovered CryptoProvider implementations by the new CryptoProvider::order() (descending) and to no longer throw when multiple providers are present; it now selects the first and logs the rest as ignored (common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java). This is a notable behavioral change in provider resolution and depends on newly introduced order() (common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoProvider.java) and its implementations (e.g., DefaultCryptoProvider/WildFlyElytronProvider/FIPS1402Provider). The only new test added is ECDSAAlgorithmTest for signature conversion, and there is no test covering provider selection scenarios (single provider, multiple providers, ordering/ties).
